rows.title: An admissible product has a finite coordinate normalizer
rows.statement:
Use the admissible mean-field product $q=\prod_{k=1}^m q_k$ on the finite product of sigma-finite reference spaces in [[def-variational-family-and-elbo]]. Fix a coordinate $j$ and put $v=q_{-j}$, with the singleton unit-measure convention when $m=1$. Suppose
$$h_j(x)=\int v(y)\log\gamma(x,y)\,d\mu_{-j}(y)$$
has a measurable extended-real version defined without an $\infty-\infty$ ambiguity, finite for $q_j\mu_j$-almost every $x$. Products with a zero density are zero. Then $H:=\int v\log v\,d\mu_{-j}$ is a finite real number and
$$0<c_j:=\int e^{h_j(x)}\,d\mu_j(x)\le e^H Z<\infty.$$
This establishes normalization only; the resulting product must still satisfy the separate support and absolute-log-integrability conditions before it is an admissible coordinate replacement. No convergence or global-optimum conclusion is asserted.

rows.title: Finite evidence and finite expected logs do not replace admissibility
rows.statement: There are a finite-evidence target $\gamma$ and a supported product probability density $q$ for which $\int q|\log\gamma|d\mu<\infty$ and the expected-log coordinate function is identically zero on a countably infinite counting space, but its exponential has infinite normalizer. This $q$ fails the entropy-integrability part of admissibility; finite evidence and pointwise finite expected log alone do not justify a coordinate update.

rows.title: A high ELBO alone does not certify posterior calibration
rows.statement: The numerical value of an ELBO depends on the scale of the unnormalized target. It alone is not a bound on posterior discrepancy, calibration, or downstream error. Here a calibration guarantee means a separately proved property of repeated-sampling coverage or posterior-probability calibration; it is not defined by the ELBO. Under AC, the library KL identity controls the gap $\log Z-\operatorname{ELBO}(q)$ through the reverse divergence, when that gap is known.
